title: L1-L2 rotation under eccentric compressive loading
condition: intact, eccentric compressive loading (moment + axial load)

quantity.name: ROM
quantity.definition: maximum L1 rotation relative to L2 (instrumented spatial linkage), mean +- SD (range), n=5; extension plateau reached at ~4 Nm (impingement); flexion at max applied flexion moment (~7.1 Nm); LB up to 3.1 Nm; AR at max torsion

source.authors: Schendel MJ, Wood KB, Buttermann GR, Lewis JL, Ogilvie JW
source.n: 5 specimens (human L1-L2 FSUs; facet data from 4)
source.sample: 5 fresh human L1-L2 motion segments (from T12-L3 sections); strain gauges failed in one, so facet force n=4

protocol.summary: L1 and L2 potted in PMMA; NOT pure moments: offset compressive cable loads (75/150/300 N) at lever arms 1-4 cm from an origin 1 cm anterior to the posterior VB rim give combined moment + axial load (Table 2, up to ~12 Nm FL/EX); lateral bending 50-200 N cable loads, up to 3.1 Nm; axial torsion via 5.5 cm lever arm (text: 10-40 Nm) with constant 150 N axial load. 300 N axial creep preload before testing. Capsules intact. Motion by instrumented spatial linkage.
how_to_simulate: Fix L2; apply eccentric compressive loads as in Table 2 (moment = cable load x lever arm, axial load = cable load)
Report maximum L1 rotation in flexion, extension (plateau from ~4 Nm), left/right lateral bending (<=3.1 Nm), axial rotation
Coupled: axial rotation of 0.27 deg per Nm of lateral bending moment
protocol.notes: Facet method: 4 strain gauges on external surface of right L1 inferior articular process (Buttermann 1990 technique), calibrated by point loads on a grid normal to facet surface, gauge-ratio contour method; impingement on L2 lamina identified by separate calibration points. Accuracy ~15% (Buttermann 1990), repeatability 5%. Impingement began at 4-6 Nm extension (bilinear facet load-moment). No facet load in flexion.

data.note: deg per Nm (sensitivity); left LB coupled with axial rotation loading the right facet

extraction.check_notes: All values read from rendered page.
